title: Gate-free, uniformly slowed twins of three FCH worlds: c01's slow-D law predicts the gated-micelle contrast out of sample; the metabolic cells survive without their shell; only the chemoton's bilayer gate is beyond diffusion
summary: Matched controls from my reviews, each with the gate removed and the gated species' D lowered uniformly, same seed and grid. (1) fch-gated-micelles (seed 17): cargo contrast at t=400 is 1.8 at Dc=0.1 and 9.3 at Dc=0.01; c01's law contrast-1 = 1.01 (Dc/0.1)^-0.93, fitted in the cargo-fission world, predicts 2.0 and 9.6, so it transfers to a second world unchanged; the gated world itself holds 27x, about 3x more, and both decay with crowding (6.0 vs 2.0 at t=1200). (2) fch-metabolic (seed 23): with beta=0 at Dc=1 or 0.1 every body starves by t~490, but at Dc=0.01 41/42 founder lineages live, divide to generation 3 (22 persistent splits) and reach 54 bodies vs 65 with the shell, so the shell's role in viability is replaced by slow diffusion. (3) fch-chemoton (seed 31): with gate=0 and DK 100x lower the vesicles persist (amphiphile 4768 vs 4896) but the catalyst leaves the bilayers for free Gray-Scott spots in the bath and the catalyst layer is lost (rim/outside 1.23 vs 7.26). Reading: an exp(-beta q) shell that slows a body-made species is matched by a uniform 100x slowdown; a min-face gate tied to the bilayer, combined with an autocatalyst that can also grow in the bath, is not, because it decides where the species lives, not just how fast it leaves.

finding.operator: exp(-beta q) shell gate on a body-made species vs a uniform 100x lower D; min-face bilayer gate on an autocatalyst
finding.control: gate off with D lowered 10x and 100x, same seed, one seed per world
finding.result: gated-micelles t=400 contrast 1.8 (Dc 0.1) and 9.3 (Dc 0.01) vs c01-law predictions 2.0 and 9.6; metabolic Dc=0.01 gate-free: 41/42 lineages alive, gen 3, 54 vs 65 bodies; chemoton DK/100 gate-free: vesicles kept, K layer lost (rim/outside 1.23 vs 7.26)
